blocks.text:
**But in the ratzon kadum**, mentioned above, **it's still within yourself; therefore it goes by way of circles**, so **that top thing, that encompasses everything and defines everything, is this hidden ratzon, this all-encompassing desire**, which is for yourself, and the main thing you see is yourself.

**And the first circle of it is the general ratzon and taanug for the whole hishtalshelus, which is inside of it. And this first igul is the general makif for the entire ABYA, for the whole hishtalshelus.**

phrases.en: and the *reshis hakav*, before this first circle, that little line thing
is a *hiyuli hamshacha*

phrases.he: כמו קו קצר המתצמצם מעילה לעלול,
phrases.en: which is similar to the little line that connects the *ila* to the *alul*
like from *ratzon* to *chachma*; that's just like a little line

blocks.text: **And the reshis hakav, before this first circle, that little line thing, is a hiyuli hamshacha** (a raw, general drawing forth), **which is similar to the little line that connects the ila to the alul**, the cause to the effect.

blocks.title: A hair from the brain
blocks.text: We said that the lower circle does not really reach the upper circle; it is just represented by it. That is the idea of a *kav*, a line, or a hair, when it speaks of the *tzimtzum* of hairs and lines and all these kinds of things. It always means that it represents the *etzem*: in one small point the *etzem* is carried over, but it is totally *metzumtzam* (contracted), in a way just a representation. That is the idea of the hair. The hair does come from the actual stuff of your brain, but now it is totally detached, and you do not see the connection, but there is one. Or in a *mashal*, there is one little thing that is an actual case; or if you give a *dugma* (an example) to represent everything, you take one thing and use it to represent the whole thing.

That is the main thing of a line: you take everything and pick one little point, something of the essence, and use it to represent as if that is everything. That is what happens. You take your *ratzon*, which could come out in any way, and you pick one *chachma*, one picture of what you want; really you could pick infinite pictures, but you pick one, and the connection between the two is just a little line. In the same way, this whole *ratzon kadum* is just like a little line from the *Atzmus Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*: the whole *hishtalshelus*, the whole desire for a *dira b'tachtonim*, is just one little example of how the *ratzon hamuchlat* could come out.

Because, as we said, in the *ratzon hamuchlat* there is no up and down; it is just the taste. That it was set up with ten *sefiros*, and that this is the main priority and that is the main *ratzon*, could have come out in infinite ways. So that is also a little line. The *Kav*, too, is that kind of little line, just bringing out a little thing: **like from ratzon to chachma; that's just like a little line.**

phrases.he: כך מבחינת הרשימו הנזכר לעיל נמשך קו בצמצום גדול מאד
phrases.en: so too from the *reshimu*, which has hidden in it all of G-d's taste of how He would want anything He would ever want and how He would do anything (the whole *Atzmus Ein Sof* is hidden there), comes out one little *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: דהגם שהרשימו הוא בא בהגבלה כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: even though we said that the *reshimu* was very limited, it's already like a *metzumtzam* thing

phrases.he: אבל הוא מבחינת עולם האין סוף על כל פנים,
phrases.en: it's still the world of the *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: רק שהוא בחינת האחרונה שנעשה בקיצור כו'
phrases.en: It's just like the end of the *Ein Sof*, which is made like in a short way

blocks.text: **So too from the reshimu, which has hidden in it all of G-d's taste of how He would want anything He would ever want and how He would do anything (the whole Atzmus Ein Sof is hidden there), comes out one little ratzon kadum**, in a very great contraction.

**Even though we said that the reshimu was very limited, it's already like a metzumtzam thing, it's still the world of the Ein Sof.** "So a zero in the world of the *Ein Sof* is more infinite than an infinity in the world of an *igul*."

The *Atzmus Ein Sof* is like a guy who has a *ratzon hamuchlat*, a certain taste, which is already the last level, *Kadmon*: He already chose to reveal Himself in a certain way, which is like a taste.

But even the particular way He is going to reveal Himself, *Kadmon*, is still in the way of a taste, still totally infinite compared to coming out into the world. At the level of *Kadmon*, where He picks a certain taste, a *ratzon hamuchlat*, it is because He feels that that style reveals Himself; He feels Himself in it. And even when He is *metzamtzem* His taste and it comes out as just a *reshimu*, where He totally hides Himself, so that all that is left are those choices of His style and taste, without seeing Him in them, without seeing how it is Him, just the choices: that is the *reshimu*. You just have all those things.

But even all of that is still far more infinite than any particular *hishtalshelus*, like making a house, because there is no up and down there yet. The bathroom drapes could be the main thing, and the house need not be; you could want the whole house for the bathroom drapes. But in the *reshimu* he already knows: if you ask him, "How would you want your house?" he will be able to tell you, because it is all there. To actually want to have a house, though, you need the *Kav*, the *tzimtzum* of the *Kav*. The *Kav* has to pull out and measure which thing he is going to bring out and in what order. That is what the *Kav* does: it measures out how it should come out.

So the *Kav* measured out that he is going to want a house, and that is the main thing; the other things will be secondary, the details of the house and what you have to do to get it. The *Kav* measures out and says, "Okay, so I want a home. That's my goal, a home." From that comes the whole thing of "I want a home," which automatically includes wanting to do whatever he will need to do to get the home. Then it goes to *yosher*: when he actually decides to do it, he goes and actually starts getting a job and working, whatever he has to do to get a home.

The *Kav* is *chozer u'meir*: it reveals the light again a little bit. The *Kav* always means your choice, so it reveals you again, because you are choosing which way to bring it out; you are measuring it, and you see that you are measuring. So you have to pick.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: For example, in the *mashal* of the teacher. The *reshimu* in the teacher is all the knowledge he has in his memory, facts that are in a way separate from him: there is him, and there are the things he knows. All the things in his memory, even though he is not thinking about them right now, are there in a hidden way; that is like the *reshimu*. He stops thinking about anything, so now you do not see his mind involved with those things; they are just there in a hidden way. Now the *Kav* is that he measures out which students he is teaching and which subjects, and how he picks which explanations to bring out. The explanations that come out now were measured out by him, so now you see a kind of *gilui ohr* (revealed light), because it is revealed in his mind.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 61 opens by going on with the reshimu and the Kav (lines 47-48), with the mashal of the teacher, before it rereads line 48.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: It is like a person thinking about deep things, with all his knowledge and understanding coming into play. Then he makes a *tzimtzum*: he puts it all away, clears his mind and thinks about nothing, and gives his full attention to the students. Then he takes out his *kav* and measures the students, and chooses which things to bring out and in which order to put them together, an idea he will be able to explain to them in a way they will understand. And he picks the *meshalim*: if the guy likes tennis, he picks tennis *meshalim*; if he likes hunting, hunting *meshalim*; if he likes cars, car *meshalim*. He picks everything: which idea to explain according to the student's level and what he needs, the *kelim* (vessels) of which explanations to put it into, which *meshalim* to use, and then he puts it all together and explains it to him.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 61 opens by going on with the reshimu and the Kav (lines 47-48), with the mashal of the teacher, before it rereads line 48.

blocks.text: The *Atzmus* is not a desire to do something; it is just to be yourself. When it comes to deciding that you want to be somebody who is doing something, that is the *sof maaseh* of the *machshava* of the *Ein Sof*, the end of *Kadmon*: you associate yourself with doing things in a certain way, to express yourself. You want to leave an impression of yourself in the world, and that is the idea of a *reshimu*, an impression. You make the *tzimtzum* in order to make a *gilui* that is separate from yourself and yet reflects on you. That is the idea of the *reshimu*: you create the concept of an impression you could make on other people, so that the fact that you chose that this idea should come out this way reveals you, even though it is separate from you.

blocks.title: A painter's signature
blocks.text: That is the idea of your choice. You pick a certain style or a certain taste, and now if something is done that way, it is like a signature. Different painters each have their character: you take one look and say, "Oh, I know who did that." That is the idea of a *reshimu*, an impression, an imprint left from the person.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 61 opens by going on with the reshimu and the Kav (lines 47-48), with the mashal of the teacher, before it rereads line 48.

blocks.title: The teacher
blocks.text: So in a teacher, the desire to teach is the desire for a *reshimu*: you want to be able to leave an impression of your intellect in somebody else's mind, to be able to affect them. So now you hide your intellect, what you think about, and you reveal the *koach hagvul* (the power of limitation), the ability to make the intellect separate from you, so that it does not have to be in your mind: you make it into ideas that are separate from you. But really it is not separate from you; really it is you. You cannot really separate the ideas from the person who thought them up. But you make it as if it is something separate, and then you are able to give it over to somebody else.

blocks.text: Even though the *reshimu* comes in a very limited way, it is still of the *Ein Sof*. The *reshimu* is the *koach hagvul* of the *Ein Sof*, but it is still infinite. It is every possible limited thing that could seem separate, that G-d could make, and there are still infinite different things there. It is not one particular *gvul* (limit); it is every possible *gvul* that could be. **It's just like the end of the Ein Sof, which is made like in a short way.** But it is still infinite.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן להיות רצון קדום
phrases.en: but to have the *ratzon kadum*

phrases.he: שהוא בא לכלל השפעה חוץ מעולם האין סוף
phrases.en: which is already outside of the world of the *Ein Sof*

phrases.he: רק שהוא היולי כולל הכל כו'
phrases.en: even though the *ratzon kadum* is a *hiyuli* that includes everything within our world

phrases.he: על כן נמשך דרך קו קצר כו'
phrases.en: Therefore, it has to come through a short *Kav*

blocks.text: **But to have the ratzon kadum, which is already outside of the world of the Ein Sof**: you already chose the one particular *ratzon* for this world, this *hishtalshelus*. Only it is *hiyuli* and includes everything: **even though the ratzon kadum is a hiyuli that includes everything within our world**, it is already a *prat* outside of the *Atzmus*, compared to before the *tzimtzum*.

**Therefore, it has to come through a short Kav.** To jump from the *reshimu* of the *koach*, which is at the end of the *Ein Sof*, to the beginning of the *hishtalshelus*, you need it to come as just a little *kav*, finite, one thing representing the whole *etzem*: you just pick out one little thing of it.

blocks.question: Is the kav katzar itself the ratzon kadum?
blocks.text: No: the *kav katzar* (the short line) is what was discussed in chapters 14 and 15, and the first *igul* that the *Kav* makes is the *ratzon kadum*. That is what we were explaining: for the *ratzon kadum* to come out from the *ratzon hamuchlat*, you have to have first the *tzimtzum*, which leaves the *reshimu* of the *ratzon hamuchlat*, and then the *Kav*. The first *igul*, the great *igul*, the *ratzon kadum*, the general *makif* of the world of *Beriya*, and all kinds of other names. Sometimes we call it the *machshava kduma* of *Adam Kadmon*, but it depends on what you are talking about.

sections.title: Up and down begin with the Kav; of the Essence above it nothing can be said
sections.summary: The *Kav* only makes an up and a down, taking one little detail of the will and connecting it to *chachma*. In the world of the *Ein Sof* there is no up and down, only simple unity, the way a person's taste is the person; so it cannot be spoken of, and only the *Kav* and *Adam Kadmon*, the cause of all causes, can be grasped. The *tzimtzum* is a jump, not a line, which is why the Essence is called holy, and why *Adam Kadmon* is a man while of the Essence it says, "He is not a man."

phrases.en: this is what it says in the Tree of Life

phrases.he: דכל עיקר הארת הקו אינו רק להיות בחינת מעלה ומטה
phrases.en: that the whole main purpose of the *Kav* is just to make an up and a down
like in the ten *sefiros*

blocks.text: **This is what it says in the Tree of Life** ("yeah, that's a book"): **that the whole main purpose of the Kav is just to make an up and a down, like in the ten sefiros**, down to the final deed. What the *Kav* does is say that the *Keser* should be on top, then comes a *chachma*, and under it a *bina*. The way it does it is that it takes the *ratzon*, takes just one little *prat* of it, and connects that to the *chachma*. So now the *chachma* represents just this one little *prat* of the *Keser*.

blocks.text: **But in the world of the Ein Sof**, since there is none of that *Kav* business going on, **there's not even an up and down.** Even with all the *tzimtzumim*, it all stays the same, all on the same level, still totally infinite, the *Atzmus* of the *Ein Sof*.

**It's just completely an achdus pshuta** (simple unity), **just one simple thing**: the *gilui* of G-d exactly the way He is. In you, it is you; it is just you. Your taste is you. If you look in books about style, in writing and things like that, they will all tell you that the taste is the person. The style is the person; it is not a separate thing.

**Even though He estimated what's going to be**, and made something like a taste, **it's all within yourself.** It is not that you were actually thinking about the particular things that were going to be; you just chose a certain taste for yourself, which is really you: you decided you are going to be a certain kind of person. That **is still completely infinite.**

blocks.text: That is why they have so much trouble explaining style. They cannot really tell you what it is. All they can tell you is that if you want to get it out, you should not think about it. Just think about the *sof maaseh*, and it will come out *mimeila* (by itself), because as long as you are doing it, it has to come out, because it is you. So it is going to be there by itself. But if you try to bring it out, you actually cover it up and make a *kelipa* (a husk) over it.

**Only in the Kav can you speak**, and in *Adam Kadmon*, which is the first source of the whole *hishtalshelus*. That first source can come to be grasped through the many stages of the *hishtalshelus*: **that can be understood after a lot of hishtalshelus**, down to the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* in *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*. You understand **how the sefiros of Atzilus are mislabesh in Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya**, and from that you can understand it.

Since it is called the cause of all causes, **because it's still the cause of all causes**, it still comes in a way of *ila v'alul* (cause and effect), so it is somehow represented at the end; **or it's called the origin**, *Kadmon*.

blocks.text: **But Atzmus Ein Sof, no thought can grasp it**, not even the *machshava kduma*. **Even the first thought of the ratzon kadum totally does not capture the Atzmus, because then the Ein Sof is totally separate. It's called completely kadosh** (holy). Why is it called *kadosh*? **Because of the tzimtzum.**

Because of the *tzimtzum*, there is no *kav* connecting them. Between before the *tzimtzum* and after the *tzimtzum* there is a jump; that is not a line. In the rest of the *hishtalshelus*, what He does is take whatever He wants to reveal and pick one little part, and make that like everything. On all the other levels you pick one swimming pool, one shape, one material and one place, and that really is a little thing of the *etzem* of what you want. But in the first *tzimtzum* you hid everything, so it is not coming through at all. You went from being you to being something outside of you, and that's it. You hid yourself; you did not pick a little thing of yourself.

blocks.text: But **the ratzon kadum is called His great name**: *shmo* (His name) is the *gematria* (numerical value) of *ratzon*; **in other words, it's His big desire.** And this is the meaning of *Yehei shmei rabba mevarach*.

There is a *kavana* you are supposed to have in *Yehei shmei rabba mevarach*: if you have it, it tears up decrees of seventy years. What is the *kavana*? That G-d's great name should be revealed in the world, drawn down into the world. What is His great name? The *ratzon* for the *dira b'tachtonim*, for *Moshiach*. So if a person connects to that *ratzon*, the spreading of the wellsprings and everything like that, it tears up all decrees, because that is the main goal.

blocks.text: As is known, **Adam Kadmon is called Adam d'Beriya**, as will be explained. **But about Atzmus Ein Sof, it says ki lo adam hu: it's not a person already.** As is known from the *kavanos* of *Nishmas Kol Chai*: **Adam Kadmon is already like a thing of a person, and it's like the soul of creation**, but higher than that you cannot call it a person at all, because that was a total jump.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between *igulim* and *yosher*, and how does drawing the circles without lifting the pen show what the beginning of the *Kav* does?
In what sense is the *ratzon kadum* already revealed, and in what sense is it still hidden? What do the teenager whose parents cramp his style and the song in your head show?
Why does every last detail, the bathroom drapes or a blade of grass, matter to the first will, and in what way is the last deed first in thought?
Why can the reasons never reach the will? Explain with the kid who wants a bike and with the bribe.
What changes when the will for oneself comes to be done in actual fact, and why does the *sof maaseh* go from the flimsiest circle to the top?
Why can even *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* not be spoken of, and why is the *tzimtzum* called a jump and not a line?
